#  11189 - Environmental Issues in Africa. Visible and Less Visible Challenges Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **11189 - module is no longer offered from SS 2018**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **Environmental Issues in Africa. Visible and Less Visible Challenges**  |  
|  Umweltbelange in Afrika. Sichtbare und weniger sichtbare Herausforderungen   |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 2 - Environment and Natural Sciences   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Prof. Dr. Dr.h.c. (NMU, UA) Schmidt, Michael 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  On special announcement   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  | Environment – not only a technical topic. Understanding of social, ethical and political connections in so-called development countries; facilitating decision making (for future work and research); introduction to basic facts, ideas and problems of Africa  |  
| Contents:  | 
  * Introduction into environmental history; environment in pre-colonial, colonial and post-colonial Africa
  * Mobility in Africa. Environment as push – and pull factors (‚voluntary‘ and ‚non-voluntary‘ migrations); refugees; urbanization/megacities
  * Anthropogenic environmental problems and attempts to solve them (waste disposal; waste exports/imports; contamination; soil degradation)
  * Oil in Africa: blessing or curse ? (Examples from various countries)
  * Challenges of the West African coasts
  * Climate Change and Africa Optional: Gwynne Dyer, Schlachtfeld Erde. Klimakriege im 21. Jahrhundert. (Summarizing and commenting)
  * Natural parks: from foreign hunters‘ paradise to ecological nature reserves
  * Special subjects: ‚chickens of death‘ (imported meat products); land grabbing – the new colonization?
  * Search for historical and environmental identity: museums in Africa
  * African Responses and initiatives – consequences of an unbalanced world economic order

 |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | None  |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | None  |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Seminar / 4 Hours per Week per Semester 
  * Self organised studies / 120 Hours 

 |  
| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | 
  * Slides (via beamer)
  * Films
  * Presentations
  * Lectures (inputs)
  * Selected books, articles etc.
  * Role plays

 |  
| Module Examination:  | Prerequisite + Final Module Examination (MAP)  |  
| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  | Prerequisite: 
  * one essay (8-12 pages) or
  * one presentation (15 minutes) or
  * one lecture minutes (2-3 pages)

Final module examination:
  * written examination, 180 min.

The form of the prerequesite will be announced in the first lesson.  |  
| Evaluation of Module Examination:  | Performance Verification – graded  |  
| Limited Number of Participants:  | 25  |  
| Part of the Study Programme:  | 
  * no assignment

 |
